// diagnostic

E1021

`#Inline(Always) fn` has a foreign body, and a function with a foreign body stays a call

What

`#Inline(Always) fn` has a foreign body, and a function with a foreign body stays a call

Why

`#Inline(Always)` guarantees every direct call is inlined on every tier, and the body of an `#FFI` or `#Import(c)` function is foreign code with no Jet body to copy into the caller. Sema refuses each mark that can't keep the guarantee: a call of itself or a cycle of marked calls (E0917), a use as a value (E0918), a body over the size ceiling (E0919), `#Scrub` (E1016), a read of `context.trace` (E1017) and a foreign body (E1021)

Fix

Drop `#Inline(Always)` from the function with the foreign body.

Worked example

First UI snapshot mentioning E1021: tests/ui/inline_always_foreign.stderr.

Error [jet.InlineAlwaysForeign]: `increment` has a foreign body, so `#Inline(Always)` cannot expand it
  --> tests/ui/inline_always_foreign.jet:5:3
    |
  5 | #[Inline(Always), Unsafe("register-only increment"), FFI(asm)]
    |   ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
 Why: The body of an `#FFI(asm)` function is foreign code, not Jet: each call goes to that code, and there is no Jet body to copy into the caller. `#Inline(Always)` guarantees that every direct call is inlined on every tier, or the program is refused: sema refuses a function that calls itself or closes a cycle of marked calls (E0917), one used as a value (E0918), one over the size ceiling (E0919), a `#Scrub` routine (E1016), one that reads `context.trace` (E1017) and one with a foreign body (E1021).
 Fix: Drop `#Inline(Always)`; a function with a foreign body stays a call.
More: jet-lang.dev/e/E1021
